s1.syndrome_frame: Gradual onset of a painless, firm, and nonpulsatile mass in the thigh, fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin, with no signs of inflammation or neurovascular impairment
salient_findings: Firm, nonpulsatile mass in the left medial thigh
Mass is fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin
CT scan shows a well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass with internal septations
key_facts: 18-month-old girl
Swelling in the left medial thigh
Mass has enlarged gradually over six months
Painless mass
No history of trauma or infection
Firm, nonpulsatile mass measuring approximately 10 cm
No signs of inflammation, neurovascular impairment, or inguinal lymphadenopathy
Laboratory tests are unremarkable
CT scan shows a well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass in the left anteromedial compartment of the proximal thigh
MRI confirms a fatty-appearing, well-circumscribed mass with internal septations

differentials: Giant cell tumor of soft tissue
Intra-abdominal desmoplastic small round cell tumor
per_call: Giant cell tumor of soft tissue
Intra-abdominal desmoplastic small round cell tumor

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: The mass is described as a firm, nonpulsatile, and painless mass with a fatty appearance on imaging, consistent with a lipoma

shortlist.label: Liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely given the age and lack of aggressive features, liposarcoma remains a consideration due to the large size of the mass

shortlist.label: Atypical lipomatous tumor
shortlist.why_kept: The imaging characteristics and gradual growth pattern could also suggest an atypical lipomatous tumor, a type of lipoma with potential for local recurrence

shortlist.label: Lipoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Given the patient's young age, lipoblastoma, a rare tumor of immature fat cells, is a plausible, albeit less common, diagnosis

shortlist.label: Intramuscular lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: The mass's location within the thigh muscle and its characteristics on imaging could also be consistent with an intramuscular lipoma

raw.rationale: The patient's age and the characteristics of the mass, including its gradual enlargement, painless nature, and fatty appearance on imaging, are consistent with lipoblastoma, a rare benign tumor of adipose tissue that typically occurs in children under the age of 3.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipomas are more common in adults and tend to be smaller and less likely to grow rapidly.

rejected.label: Liposarcoma
rejected.why: Liposarcomas are malignant tumors that are rare in children and typically exhibit more aggressive features on imaging, such as invasion of surrounding tissues.

rejected.label: Atypical lipomatous tumor
rejected.why: Atypical lipomatous tumors are rare in children and often have a more complex appearance on imaging, with a higher risk of local recurrence.

rejected.label: Intramuscular lipoma
rejected.why: Intramuscular lipomas can occur in children but are less likely to present as a large, rapidly growing mass in the thigh.
